claims.title: Any model-network principal can read customer features from the passwordless Redis store
claims.description: `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features` has `authentication: none`, allowing an honest-but-curious insider or an attacker who gains any foothold in `boundary:model-network` to read `store:feature-store` rather than being limited to requests mediated by `process:model-server`. The store holds per-customer account-age and spend-band data, so the attacker can enumerate customer PII and financial profiling data in bulk. Those profiles can subsequently be used to identify and target high-value customers through the inference-serving path.

grounds.text: Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network. The features include account age and spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features` states authentication is absent, although the attacker must first gain model-network access. Impact is high because `store:feature-store` is confidential and tagged `pii` and `financial`, and passwordless read access can expose the per-customer corpus.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated, least-privilege Redis access
mitigations.detail: Configure authentication for `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features`, use a distinct service identity for `process:model-server`, and restrict it to only the required keys and commands.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the feature-store connection
mitigations.detail: Enable TLS for Redis and verify `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features` so a model-network foothold cannot passively collect feature reads.

claims.title: A storage-layer copy of the feature store exposes customer profiles if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:feature-store` is confidential, contains per-customer account-age and spend-band data, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If that attribute resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker or over-privileged operator obtaining storage-layer access or an operational copy of the Redis data can read the customer feature corpus without using `process:model-server` or the passwordless Redis read path. The resulting PII and financial profiling data enables targeted abuse of customers reached through the inference system. This is conditional on the unverified at-rest encryption state, not an assertion that encryption is absent.

grounds.text: The features include account age and spend bands per customer.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `encryption_at_rest` on `store:feature-store`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:store:feature-store:encryption_at_rest`: obtaining storage-layer access is a prerequisite, but the relevant control is unverified. Impact is high because the confidential `store:feature-store` is tagged `pii` and `financial`, and a raw copy can disclose customer data in bulk.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt Redis data and all operational copies at rest
mitigations.detail: Verify the current state, then enforce managed-key encryption for `store:feature-store` and any persistence, backup, snapshot, or export associated with it; restrict key use and export permissions.

claims.title: Model artifact publication may be deniable to an individual engineer
claims.description: `entity:ml-engineer` can publish a model artifact through `flow:ml-engineer-to-model-registry:publish-artifact` into `store:model-registry`, but that flow's `authentication` is unknown and the source specifically raises the possibility of a shared group account. If publication uses that shared identity and no individual, immutable change record is retained, an engineer who publishes a malicious or unapproved artifact can deny doing so because the available evidence identifies at most the group account. This is conditional on resolving the unknown authentication and audit-record design; it does not assert that the account is shared. Second-order: `process:model-server` loads artifacts from `store:model-registry` at startup, so an unresolvable publication dispute affects accountability for the model serving all downstream inference requests.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:flow:ml-engineer-to-model-registry:publish-artifact:authentication`: publication originates from `entity:ml-engineer` inside `boundary:model-network`, requiring an engineer or their credentials, but a shared group identity would make denial straightforward. Impact is high because `store:model-registry` holds `business-critical-data` and `process:model-server` loads its artifacts at startup, extending an unresolvable publication dispute to the served model.

mitigations.summary: Use individually attributable artifact-publishing identities
mitigations.detail: Replace any shared group account on `flow:ml-engineer-to-model-registry:publish-artifact` with individual, short-lived engineer credentials and record the verified principal rather than a self-reported username.

mitigations.summary: Create immutable artifact provenance records
mitigations.detail: Record each publication's acting principal, artifact digest, timestamp, previous version, approval outcome, and signature in append-only or WORM audit storage separate from `store:model-registry`; require `process:model-server` to load only approved, signed artifacts.

claims.title: Unverified artifact publication can plant a malicious model loaded at startup
claims.description: If `flow:ml-engineer-to-model-registry:publish-artifact`'s unknown authentication permits an insufficiently controlled or shared publisher identity, an attacker able to use that write path can plant a modified model artifact in `store:model-registry`. `process:model-server` loads artifacts from this store at startup without integrity verification, so the planted artifact can alter model-server behavior and every inference request it processes. This is conditional on the unresolved publisher authentication, not an assertion that access control is absent.

mitigations.summary: Restrict and authenticate artifact publication

mitigations.summary: Verify signed artifacts before loading
mitigations.detail: Require `process:model-server` to verify a trusted signature and immutable artifact digest before loading from `store:model-registry`; reject unsigned or unexpected versions.

claims.title: An on-path attacker can rewrite requests forwarded into the model network
claims.description: `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` crosses from `boundary:serving-edge` into `boundary:model-network`, has `authentication: none`, and has unverified `protocol` and `encryption_in_transit` attributes. If the unresolved transport protection does not provide authenticated integrity, an attacker positioned on this cross-zone path can alter an otherwise legitimate inference request before `process:model-server` receives it. The model server then performs inference on attacker-modified content; the altered request can also drive use of incorrect customer-feature context through `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features`. This threat is conditional on the unverified protocol and transport-integrity state, while the absence of flow authentication is stated.

grounds.text: There is no auth between the gateway and the model server; the model network is meant to be reachable only from the gateway.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `protocol` on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`, `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request:encryption_in_transit`: the flow crosses a trust boundary and has no stated authentication, but the attacker still needs an on-path or routing position. Impact is high because altered requests are trusted by `process:model-server`, which is tagged `business-critical-data` and `availability-critical`, affecting its inference behavior.

mitigations.summary: Use mutually authenticated transport for the gateway-to-model-server flow
mitigations.detail: Set a verified protocol and require mTLS with certificate identity validation on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`, providing both peer authentication and authenticated encryption.

mitigations.summary: Bind forwarded requests to the gateway
mitigations.detail: Have `process:inference-gateway` sign or otherwise integrity-bind request payloads and have `process:model-server` verify the signature before accepting forwarded inference requests.

claims.title: A compromise of the internet-facing gateway crosses into the unauthenticated model network
claims.description: An attacker who obtains code execution or network control of `process:inference-gateway` inherits its network-position access on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`. That flow crosses from the serving edge into the model network, but `process:model-server` accepts it with no authentication, so the attacker can invoke the internal model-serving surface without holding authority in `boundary:model-network`. This is a zone-escape escalation: the gateway's position, rather than an authenticated caller identity, is sufficient to reach `process:model-server`. Second-order, the invoked model workload normally reads customer features through `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features`, reaching `store:feature-store` data containing customer account-age and spend-band information.

claims.title: Inference requests may be intercepted on the unverified internet-facing transport path

If transport encryption is not actually enforced for every segment, an attacker able to observe the public-network path or a terminating intermediary can intercept request PII before it reaches `process:inference-gateway`. The captured prompts can reveal user-provided content and help an attacker target the calling services or their users.

If the unverified hop is plaintext, a compromised workload, sidecar, or network observer positioned between `process:inference-gateway` and `process:model-server` can intercept customer request data. The observed request identifiers and content can then be correlated with `process:model-server`'s feature lookups to target particular customers in later attacks.

claims.title: Raw end-user prompts are exposed from inference-log storage if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `process:inference-gateway` records every request and response in `store:inference-log`, which is confidential, tagged `pii`, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If at-rest encryption is not enabled, a storage-layer attacker or over-privileged operator with an operational copy can read raw prompts and model responses directly, bypassing the gateway's API-key path. The disclosed prompts may contain whatever end users typed, enabling subsequent targeting of those users or their calling teams. This threat is conditional on the unverified encryption-at-rest attribute.

mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for `store:inference-log`, including exports, backups, and snapshots, with tightly scoped access to keys and data-export operations.

mitigations.detail: Redact or tokenize prompt fields before `process:inference-gateway` writes `flow:inference-gateway-to-inference-log:write-request-log`, and retain raw content only when explicitly required.

claims.title: Model artifacts may be disclosed from registry storage if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:model-registry` holds model artifacts and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If the bucket's storage and operational copies are unencrypted, a storage-layer attacker or over-privileged operator can read model artifacts without authenticating as `process:model-server` or an `entity:ml-engineer`. Disclosure of the model artifacts exposes business-critical model intellectual property and can help an attacker understand the serving system before targeting `process:model-server`. This is a conditional finding about the unresolved at-rest encryption state.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce registry encryption at rest
mitigations.detail: Establish the encryption state of `store:model-registry`, require managed-key encryption for the bucket and its copies, and limit decrypt and export permissions to the artifact publication and serving identities.

claims.title: A stolen long-lived team API key can be used to act as a calling service
claims.description: An internet attacker who obtains a per-team API key can present it on `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request` and act as `entity:calling-service` to `process:inference-gateway`. Because the key never expires or rotates, possession remains sufficient for impersonation until it is manually replaced. Second-order: accepted requests are forwarded by `process:inference-gateway` to `process:model-server`, allowing the impostor to consume the inference path under the victim team's identity.

grounds.text: Keys are issued per calling team and we have never expired one.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` and a never-expiring API key remains replayable once obtained, although key acquisition is still a prerequisite. Impact is medium because the impersonator reaches the internet-facing `process:inference-gateway` and its downstream `process:model-server`, which is tagged `business-critical-data` and `availability-critical`.

mitigations.summary: Replace permanent team API keys with short-lived audience-bound credentials
mitigations.detail: Use workload identity federation or short-lived OAuth/OIDC access tokens bound to `process:inference-gateway`, with expiry, audience validation, and per-team scopes on `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request`.

mitigations.summary: Rotate and contain any remaining API keys
mitigations.detail: Until migration is complete, rotate keys regularly, issue a distinct key per calling workload rather than only per team, monitor anomalous use, and support prompt revocation.

claims.title: A foothold at the serving edge can impersonate the gateway to the model server
claims.description: An attacker who gains network reachability in `boundary:serving-edge` can send requests over `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` while posing as `process:inference-gateway`, because `process:model-server` accepts the crossing based on network position rather than a verified caller identity. Second-order: the model server processes the forged requests and can read customer features from `store:feature-store`, which carries `pii` and `financial` assets, so the impersonation reaches more than the edge-to-model hop.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the flow is a derived crossing from `boundary:serving-edge` to `boundary:model-network` with authentication stated absent, but exploitation requires a foothold or request-origin capability in the serving-edge zone. Impact is medium because forged requests reach `process:model-server`, tagged `business-critical-data` and `availability-critical`, and can trigger its feature reads involving `pii` and `financial` assets.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate gateway-to-model-server requests independently of network location
mitigations.detail: Require mTLS or workload-identity tokens on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`, and configure `process:model-server` to authorize only the specific gateway workload identity.

mitigations.summary: Bind requests to the authenticated gateway identity

Second-order: `process:model-server` loads registry artifacts at startup without integrity verification, so an artifact accepted under the forged engineer identity can affect the business-critical inference workload. If HTTPS is not verified as providing authenticated transport integrity for this deployed path, an attacker able to occupy the network path can alter end-user text or request parameters before the gateway accepts them. Second-order, `process:inference-gateway` forwards the modified request on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` and records the attacker-modified request and response through `flow:inference-gateway-to-inference-log:write-request-log`. This is a needs-information threat about the unverified transport attribute, not a claim that HTTPS is plaintext.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce TLS integrity on the public request flow
mitigations.detail: Confirm that `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request` uses TLS 1.2+ with valid certificate verification and authenticated encryption from each calling service to `process:inference-gateway`.

mitigations.detail: Apply server-side schema and length validation in `process:inference-gateway` before forwarding requests, and bind caller identity and request metadata to the authenticated API-key principal.

rejected_claims.title: Unauthenticated Redis access enables alteration of customer features
rejected_claims.description: An attacker who gains a foothold in `boundary:model-network` can directly alter records in `store:feature-store`, because the Redis access described by `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features` has `authentication: none`. The attacker can rewrite account-age or spend-band values for targeted customers rather than merely read them. Second-order, `process:model-server` consumes those altered features during inference, causing manipulated model inputs and potentially incorrect decisions or outputs for affected customers.

grounds.text: Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network.

verdict.reason: The model states that the model server's flow to the feature store performs a read, but it does not state that a model-network foothold has write access or that the Redis store accepts writes from that attacker. The assertion that the attacker can directly alter records is unsupported.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium: `absent:flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features:authentication` makes writes straightforward once an attacker has a model-network foothold, but that internal foothold remains a prerequisite. Impact is medium because `store:feature-store` is confidential and tagged `pii` and `financial`, and its altered customer features are consumed by `process:model-server` for inference.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated, least-privilege Redis access
mitigations.detail: Configure `store:feature-store` to require a distinct authenticated identity for `process:model-server`, limit that identity to required read operations, and deny direct writes except to explicitly authorized writers.

mitigations.summary: Protect feature integrity before inference

rejected_claims.title: API-key holder can flood GPU inference capacity through the public gateway
rejected_claims.description: An attacker who holds any valid calling-team API key can send high-rate or computationally demanding requests over `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request` from `boundary:public-internet`. `process:inference-gateway` forwards each request on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` to `process:model-server`, where the actual GPU-backed inference runs. Without documented per-key rate limits, request-cost budgets, input-complexity bounds, or concurrency shedding, the attacker spends requests while the service consumes scarce gateway workers and GPU inference capacity. Second-order, saturation of `process:model-server` prevents legitimate product teams from obtaining inference; because both it and `process:inference-gateway` are tagged `availability-critical`, the outage affects the serving path rather than only the attacking caller.
